title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from the neighbouring pages. X and Y are smooth projective varieties and m = dim Y. B_X = Pic^0(X) is the Picard variety of X, A_Y = Alb(Y) is the Albanese variety of Y, and S_Y : Cyc_0(Y)^{deg 0} → A_Y is the summation (Albanese) map. A correspondence class 𝔷 (written z) on X×Y sends divisor classes on X to 0-cycle classes on Y. The previous page states the proposition. There is a unique homomorphism of abelian varieties u : B_X → A_Y with u(cl(D)) = S_Y(^t𝔷(D)) whenever ^t𝔷(D) is defined. The induced map on ℓ-adic H^1 is compatible with a cohomological correspondence built from the class of 𝔷 and a Lefschetz-type class γ^{[...]}(ξ). Finally, u depends only on the numerical class of 𝔷. The proof there reduces to constructing u with the cycle-theoretic property; result '1.7' then identifies it.

This page constructs u directly, without cohomology.
(i) It suffices to work with classes modulo linear (rational) equivalence, or even Albanese equivalence. The reason is that S_Y kills degree-0 0-cycles that are linearly equivalent to 0. Hence one need not worry about whether intersection (cup) products of actual cycles are defined. It is enough to study d ↦ S_Y(𝔷(d)) for divisor classes d.
(ii) Let Θ ∈ A^1(X×B_X) be the canonical (Poincaré) class, normalised so that Θ(o) = 0. Let π : Y×X×B_X → Y×B_X be the projection. Intersection theory gives 𝔷(Θ(b)) ≃ C(b), where C = π_*((1_Y×Θ)·(𝔷×1_{B_X})) ∈ Z^m(Y×B_X). C is a family of 0-cycles on Y parametrised by B_X.
(iii) Since Θ(o) = 0, 𝔷(Θ(b)) = 𝔷(Θ((b)−(o))).
(iv) Result 1.1 is the universal property of the Albanese variety for families of 0-cycles: a cycle C on Y×T induces a homomorphism A_T → A_Y. Applied with T = B_X (so A_T = B_X), it gives u : B_X → A_Y with S_Y(C((b)−(o))) = u(b), i.e. S_Y(𝔷(Θ(b))) = u(b).

The next page checks the cohomological compatibility via 1.6, linearity in 𝔷, and the numerical-equivalence statement. It also sketches a variant: the divisorial correspondence Θ_Y ∘ 𝔷 ∘ ^tΘ_X on B_X×B_Y, read as a map B_X → B_Y^* ≅ A_Y.

This is the classical construction of the homomorphism Pic^0(X) → Alb(Y) induced by a correspondence, as in Weil, Matsusaka and Lang. It sits inside Grothendieck's programme of comparing the action of correspondences on Pic/Alb with their action on ℓ-adic H^1, as needed for the standard conjectures.
errors: No substantive error. Minor gap: 'C(b)' (the specialisation of the cycle C at a point b) and the identity 𝔷(Θ(b)) ≃ C(b) need either a refined Gysin pullback to the fibre over b, or a restriction to b where the intersections are proper. Working modulo rational equivalence, as Grothendieck suggests, covers this. It is also implicit that u is a homomorphism (it sends o to 0, and rigidity of maps between abelian varieties does the rest) and that 1.1 accepts a cycle class rather than a cycle.

ideas.what: Homomorphism Pic^0(X) → Alb(Y) induced by a correspondence, constructed by restricting the Poincaré class Θ ∈ A^1(X×Pic^0 X) through 𝔷 to a family of 0-cycles on Y over Pic^0(X), then applying the universal property of Albanese
ideas.modern_name: Action of correspondences on Picard and Albanese varieties (functoriality of Pic^0/Alb under correspondences)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (theory of correspondences, 1948); Matsusaka; Lang, Abelian Varieties (1959)
ideas.where_published: Closest are FGA (Picard scheme) and Kleiman's 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (in Dix exposés, 1968), which reports Grothendieck's standard-conjecture framework

ideas.what: Reduction to cycle classes modulo rational/Albanese equivalence, using that S_Y kills rationally trivial 0-cycles, so existence of intersection products of actual cycles is irrelevant
Variant (next page): u as the divisorial correspondence Θ_Y ∘ 𝔷 ∘ ^tΘ_X on B_X×B_Y, via A_Y ≅ B_Y^*
ideas.modern_name: Duality between Picard and Albanese varieties; divisorial correspondences

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but classical construction of the map Pic^0(X) → Alb(Y) induced by a correspondence. It serves as a lemma toward the comparison with ℓ-adic H^1 in Grothendieck's standard-conjecture notes. Nothing beyond Weil/Lang-era material appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'z' throughout is a fraktur 𝔷 (the correspondence class), consistent with the next page.
'se borner à regarder d ans S_Y(z(d))' should read 'se borner à regarder d ↦ S_Y(𝔷(d))' (or 'd dans S_Y(𝔷(d))'). The 'ans' is a split word or arrow.
In C = π_*((1_Y × Θ).(𝔷 × 1_{B_X})), the first factor is written 1_Y (subscript Y under the 1).
The struck-out formula before 'S_Y(C((b)−(o))) = u(b)' is a deleted '𝔷(Θ(b))'. The final displayed line reads 'S_Y(𝔷(Θ(b))) = u(b)'.
'[-identifiant d'un point-]' is a deletion continuing onto the next line ('point' is struck out).
